items.text: Field book, AQ-41: Copper Finch starts behind the split alder in the quarry's west bay. Count seven bolts before the chain station. The pale streak below bolt four gives us a repeatable photo reference; Mara has the initial pictures.

GR-09 covers Copper Finch on Glass Ridge, a natural-protection route reached from the eastern saddle. Its key inspection feature is a detached-looking flake at the second ledge; there are no installed bolts on this line.

AQ-42 / Tin Lark: left of the quarry Finch, starting at the square drainage notch. Five bolts lead to two rings. For this inspection Tessa is tracking the right ring's movement, not the hangers along the climb.
Loose pocket note: 'Finch — return for a wider photograph before the next review.' No venue, feature, work-order number, or photographer appears on the paper.
PH-12 opening check at Plover Hall. Moon Ladder is the orange indoor training line on panel C; the rotating foothold is the third orange hold from the floor. The wall manager has the panel diagram.

AQ-41 correction. Yesterday's sketch numbered the suspect hanger as four. Counting from the ground makes it five; the pale streak remains below the actual fourth bolt. Replace the sketch, then repeat that close photograph before deciding what work the route needs.

Alder Quarry west-bay visit plan: inspect Copper Finch under AQ-41 first, then Tin Lark under AQ-42. They share the approach closure and camera tripod. The Finch's hanger close-up and the Lark's ring-station panorama are separate deliverables for that one visit.

Tin Lark return sheet: the right ring moved when unloaded; the left did not. Tessa put a purple tie on the camera bag so these photos can be matched to AQ-42. Obtain a second view of both rings together.

Moon Ladder maintenance slip: panel C's third foothold has been replaced, but the opening checklist remains unsigned until the manager tests it. Add the old hold's photograph to PH-12 so its position can be reconstructed.

Glass Ridge Finch, voice memo: approaching from the saddle, the flake makes a hollow sound near its lower edge. That is an observation for the specialist, not a clearance decision. Photograph the whole second ledge before another close-up.
The quarry Finch file needs the fifth hanger photo retaken.
The orange line on panel C still awaits manager sign-off.
Unattached voice fragment: 'The corrected sketch still needs signing; ask the person with the pictures.' The recording contains no route name or location.
Purple-bag pictures received; AQ-42 still lacks the wide station shot.
The eastern-saddle flake photos now sit in GR-09's pending folder.

Index repair: both the Alder Quarry and Glass Ridge surveys are titled Copper Finch. Add AQ-41 to the seven-bolt quarry folder and GR-09 to the eastern-saddle flake folder. The duplicate name caused a photograph to land in the wrong survey.

Plover Hall correction: the replacement foothold is orange, like the rest of Moon Ladder. 'Yellow' in my purchase note describes the supplier's packet, not a route-color change. PH-12 should continue using the orange line in the location field.

Revised Tin Lark sketch at Alder Quarry: drainage notch is triangular, not square. The start has not moved; our drawing was careless. Tessa confirmed the two-ring station in the earlier pictures, so retain those observations and amend only the approach annotation.

Mara's upload finally includes the straight-on close-up, but the oblique view catches a shadow across the metal and cannot establish whether the dark line is a surface mark. The images belong to the seven-bolt line behind the split alder. I marked the inspection incomplete and wrote a return visit into AQ-41. Nobody has signed the clearance box. We should compare the new photograph with the first visit using the pale streak as the locator, because the corrected numbering alone will be easy to misread.

Correction to GR-09 field transcription: the ledge is roughly waist high above our stance, not a waist wide. The audio says 'high'. This does not revise the route description or remove the outstanding assessment of the flake on the ridge Finch.

French release correction: the greenhouse string we marked as missing is present in the full-game bundle. Its identifier changed from guide_seed_3 to guide_graft_3. Jules verified the French line; update the lookup in the LO-FR checklist.

Lantern Orchard localization sync: LO-ES demo and LO-FR full release both consume the greenhouse button layout. The UI width correction should be checked with the Spanish short label and the French longer label before the shared screen prefab is accepted.

LO-ES issue 18: the Lantern Orchard demo teaches grafting in the greenhouse. Our Spanish glossary uses 'brote' for the new shoot. The tutorial button gets only twelve visible characters at the smallest supported window.

QE-DE puzzle note: The Quiet Engine's German boiler clues refer to a valve called Lantern. The name is etched on the mechanism, so the glossary treats it as a label rather than an instruction to light something.
Unlinked reminder: 'The wording changed; check the next package before approval.' The pasted note has no game title, language, speaker, or issue number.

SF-ES ticket: Stone Ferry's Spanish kiosk truncates the destination 'Orchard'. It is a station name inside this ferry game. The kiosk has a separate narrow-font setting that the dialogue boxes do not use.

Jules settled the winter-market address in LO-FR: use the formal form throughout the vendor exchange. The greenhouse guide remains informal. Both speakers appear in Lantern Orchard's French release, so note the speaker distinction in the glossary.

Spanish demo correction for Lantern Orchard: issue 18 was filed against the dialogue bubble, but the clipped string belongs to the greenhouse button. Keep the approved translation; first try the UI team's width fix in LO-ES.

The German boiler screen in The Quiet Engine shows the Lantern label correctly, but its tooltip swaps inlet and outlet. I linked the scene capture to QE-DE and asked the translator to compare both arrows before revising the sentence.

Spanish terminology office hours will cover LO-ES's grafting vocabulary and SF-ES's passenger-ticket correction. They are two game deliveries with one language reviewer. Send the Lantern Orchard greenhouse screenshot and the Stone Ferry kiosk screenshot in the same agenda.

Stone Ferry Spanish screenshot review: switching the kiosk to the approved narrow font restores the whole destination. The remaining ticket-printer caption still overlaps the coin icon. Track that caption under SF-ES, not the font change.
LO-ES greenhouse button fits now; capture the small-window screenshot tomorrow.
Paste from an unlabeled chat: 'Orchard still clips at narrow width; translation is approved.' No game title, locale, string identifier, or screenshot accompanies the message.
QE-DE valve tooltip approved; the German audio subtitle remains stale.
LO-FR vendor review reopened: one informal reply survived yesterday's pass.
The ferry kiosk coin-icon overlap survives in today's SF-ES build.

Chat recap for the twelve-character grafting button: the wider control fits in the small-window build, though its focus border still touches the neighboring seed icon. That observation is about Lantern Orchard's Spanish demo. The translator has already approved the word, and changing it again would disguise a layout bug. I reopened issue 18 for the UI owner and attached the exact window dimensions, along with the new screenshot showing the full button text. The screenshot should stay with the LO-ES build report.

Release-chat correction for The Quiet Engine: the stale German line is a subtitle asset, not voice audio. No recording session is needed. Rebuild the subtitle bundle for QE-DE and replay the boiler sequence with captions enabled.

LO-FR release sheet: Lantern Orchard's French full game includes the greenhouse tutorial and the winter market. Jules owns the French glossary; the first review question is whether the market vendor addresses the player formally.

Correction to the SF-ES glossary request: 'boarding pass' refers to a passenger ticket, not the kiosk's maintenance card. The scene screenshot shows the player buying a river crossing. Ask for the passenger term throughout that exchange.

MC-93 is Mount Vale School's relief map, a plaster terrain model on a wooden base. Its northeast corner is lifted, and the painted harbor bears the same generic soundings key used in several teaching aids.

MC-71 intake: Eastmere harbor wall chart, dated 1892. A tear crosses the soundings legend at lower right. The backing carries a red inventory stamp, and the hanging rod remains attached along the upper edge.
Uncaptioned desk slip: 'Eastmere needs another close photograph of the damaged lettering.' Neither an accession number nor the object's format is supplied.
MC-72 intake: Eastmere harbor pocket map, dated 1910, folded into a blue cloth case. The central fold has cracked through two harbor labels. Unlike the wall format, this object has no hanging rod.

MC-88, Briar County drainage atlas: plate seven has a brown tide mark across its marsh legend. The map uses 'Eastmere' for an inland drainage district; its bound atlas format and plate number identify the object.

Mount Vale relief map examination: the lifted plaster corner has a fine crack toward the mountain ridge. Support blocks are under the wooden base, not touching the paint. Add a side-profile image to MC-93 before discussing an adhesive.

The imaging session pairs MC-71's flat soundings legend with MC-93's raised, painted harbor key. Use the same color target for the Eastmere wall chart and Mount Vale relief map, then take an additional side view for the plaster object.

The wall chart's soundings-legend tear measures 34 millimeters after flattening the curled edge. My initial 43 millimeters included a crease. Amend the MC-71 condition diagram; no treatment decision follows from the corrected length alone.

Plate seven's tide mark is visible in both normal and transmitted-light photographs. The Briar atlas binding stays closed outside the cradle. No wet treatment has been authorized; MC-88 currently records examination and sample planning only.

Pocket Eastmere map update: the blue case is stable enough for photography. The brittle central fold still needs support during opening. Put the unfolded view and the closed-case view together in MC-72's condition record.
MC-93 corner profile uploaded; no adhesive treatment has begun yet.
MC-71 legend repair tissue sample awaits the conservator's review.
MC-88 plate-seven cradle angle reduced; the gutter now rests comfortably.
Scrap tucked under a ruler: 'Correct orientation before approving support.' There is no object name, diagram, or accompanying accession label.
The blue-case harbor map remains on the folding support.

Eastmere display planning joins MC-71, the 1892 wall chart, and MC-72, the 1910 pocket map. Photograph the same North Pier area on both for the exhibition comparison, while retaining each object's own treatment record and accession label.

School relief map correction: our first photograph was rotated, so the lifted corner was labeled southeast. The compass rose on MC-93 establishes northeast. Update the orientation arrows without changing the recorded crack outline.

Treatment journal, wall-sized Eastmere chart: the tissue trial is still on the sample sheet, not on the object. The red stamp on the backing remains visible in our photographs, and the upper hanging rod is supported on foam for the inspection. I added raking-light images of the lower-right legend because the curl made the original condition drawing hard to interpret. Those images belong to accession MC-71. The next review should consider the corrected tear measurement and the trial's appearance together before approving a repair.

Briar drainage atlas correction: the loose sheet beside plate seven is a later tracing, not plate eight. Photograph its watermark separately and update MC-88's component list. The tide-mark observation on the bound seventh plate remains unchanged.

Correction for MC-72: the crack crosses the North Pier label and the Ferry Steps label, not South Pier. My handwritten N looked like an S. Revise the diagram for the 1910 pocket map before the support design is finalized.
Message forwarded without a sender: 'Lantern Set needs the opening count checked again.' The text has no cast group, show time, or leader.

Evening call, Juniper Hall: River Steps adults perform Lantern Set at seven. Omar leads eight dancers; their opening is a circle from the kitchen-side door. Lantern props are stored in the group's black trunk.

Linden Court access rehearsal: Cedar Wheels present Turning Home. Four wheelchair dancers and four standing dancers start in two facing lines. Dev coordinates the wide turn around the central lantern prop.

Matinee call, Juniper Hall: River Steps youth present Lantern Set at two. Nia leads twelve dancers, and the opening diagonal enters from the garden-side door. The scarf basket travels with the youth group's red case.

Dockside Pavilion rehearsal: Harbor Circle seniors dance Tide Waltz with a seated opening and a supported rise on the second musical phrase. Bea coordinates the six performers and brings the blue chair markers.

Juniper Hall handover: River Steps youth's matinee Lantern Set ends before the adults' evening Lantern Set spacing call. Nia will leave the music stand for Omar. The red youth case exits through the garden door while the adult black trunk enters by the kitchen.

Omar wants the adult Lantern Set circle to open earlier so the rear pair can see the audience. Try it during the seven o'clock show's spacing call. The kitchen-side entry stays, and the black trunk should wait backstage.

Bea's Tide Waltz note: the blue chair markers are too close to the pavilion pillar. Shift the entire seated opening one marked tile toward the water-side windows, then confirm every performer is comfortable with the revised path.

Nia's matinee correction: there are eleven dancers after a withdrawal, not twelve. Leave the garden-side entry and the music unchanged; shorten the opening diagonal by one place. This updates River Steps youth's Lantern Set blocking.

Turning Home at Linden Court: Dev measured the taped turning area with the actual chairs and requested a wider gap beside the central lantern. Reposition the prop mark before the next run, then check the approach from both facing lines.
Adult black trunk delivered; Omar's evening spacing call remains outstanding.
Backstage scrap: 'Bring the spare marker tape for tomorrow's run.' No hall, performer, dance title, or coordinator is named.
Dockside blue markers moved; Bea will check the rise tomorrow.

Omar and Dev agreed to share the spare fabric lantern: River Steps adults can use it at Juniper Hall in the evening after Cedar Wheels finish Turning Home at Linden Court. Confirm collection time on both production sheets before arranging transport.
Cedar Wheels lantern mark shifted; Dev's full-group run is pending.
Youth red case packed; Nia still needs the matinee cue sheet.

Correction for River Steps adults: the seven o'clock Lantern Set has nine dancers because the understudy joins the finale. Omar updated the circle diagram. Only the finale count changes; the opening still begins with eight.

Tide Waltz correction from Harbor Circle: the rise starts on phrase three, after a repeated introduction. The earlier sheet counted the repeat as part of phrase one. Bea has annotated the score for the Dockside showcase.

Turning Home correction: the central lantern is a lightweight fabric prop, not a working lamp. The equipment list imported the wrong description. Update Cedar Wheels' Linden Court sheet so the setup team brings the fabric piece.

Rehearsal notes for the two o'clock Lantern Set: the shortened diagonal now clears the front row of chairs, but the youngest dancer loses the pause before the scarf lift. Nia wants another quiet run with the count spoken aloud. The garden-side entrance worked, and the red case has all eleven scarves. I have put these notes in the River Steps youth matinee folder so the next volunteer can find the corrected cast count alongside the blocking drawing. We have not changed the recorded music or the final pose.

MR-C visit: Cedar on Mill Roof is the unpainted hive beside the west skylight. We are recording landing-board traffic after a screen adjustment. The rooftop log has no brood-frame photography planned this week.

ML-B visit: Birch at Meadow Lane is the blue hive beside the stone bench. The ongoing task is a sequence of exterior moisture observations beneath the cover. Label each image with ML-B and the corner photographed.

OG-C visit: Cedar at Orchard Gate is the green hive beside the rain barrel. We photographed the brood pattern on frame three and saw the marked queen. The frame map is clipped inside the Orchard Gate inspection book.

OG-W visit: Willow at Orchard Gate is the yellow hive beside the gatepost. A feeder sits above the upper box. Weigh that feeder before and after the next check and record the figures on the Willow sheet.

Cedar record cleanup: prefix the Orchard Gate brood photographs with OG-C and the Mill Roof landing-board counts with MR-C. Both colonies share the name Cedar, which caused an observer to attach the rooftop weather note to the orchard frame map.

Mill Roof Cedar traffic count: wind drove the observers off the west side before the second interval. Save the first interval as incomplete, with its weather note. MR-C needs another observation under conditions that allow a full count.

Orchard Gate Cedar correction: the brood photograph is frame four when counted from the entrance side. Yesterday I counted from the rear. Amend OG-C's map so the next visit compares the same comb surface.
Unlabeled notebook corner: 'Cedar check postponed; take the camera next time.' No apiary, hive color, observation type, or record code accompanies it.

Willow feeder log, Orchard Gate: the lid was included in the first weight and excluded in the second. Those two figures cannot show consumption. Repeat using the same assembled feeder for OG-W and annotate the flawed pair.

Meadow Lane Birch: droplets appeared beneath the northeast corner of the cover during the morning look. Photograph that corner again at the next scheduled visit and record the weather; one image alone does not establish the cause.
West-skylight Cedar traffic sheet rescheduled after wind interrupted the count.
Green hive by barrel: OG-C frame-four comparison photograph still pending.
Blue hive moisture image received; ML-B weather field remains blank.
Yellow hive's assembled feeder weighed; OG-W comparison is due next visit.

Orchard Gate visit list covers Cedar OG-C and Willow OG-W. Bring the camera for Cedar's corrected frame-four comparison and the scale for Willow's assembled feeder. Both colonies are inside the same locked gate, so arrange one access slot.

MR-C caption correction: the screen adjustment was at the landing board, not the skylight. The hive remains beside the west skylight. Fix the rooftop log heading so the next observer looks at the hive entrance.
Text saved without its conversation: 'Next visit moved to morning; bring the updated sheet.' There is no colony, place, observation type, or date in the fragment.

Inspection journal for Cedar beside the Orchard Gate rain barrel: the next photograph should use the entrance-side numbering written on the revised map. A different frame would make the before-and-after comparison misleading. The marked queen was visible during the earlier visit, and the original image is still useful once its caption is corrected. I have not inferred a trend from one photograph. Put the new observation, weather note, and time of visit on the OG-C sheet, because the image filename alone says only Cedar and could be mistaken for another apiary's record.

Birch log correction: the damp corner is northwest, using the entrance as south on the site sketch. The earlier northeast label came from a mirrored phone preview. Amend ML-B's image caption and retain the original photograph.

OG-W correction: the feeder is above the lower box because Willow currently has only one box. The phrase 'upper box' came from an old form. The gatepost location and the feeder-weight procedure still identify this colony.

The installer can survey AW-H's main-house utility cupboard and AW-S's studio pottery-sink area during one appointment at 14 Alder Walk. Request two revised drawings: one for the east tiled roof job and one for the detached flat-roof studio.

LL-22 planning at 22 Linden Lane: the west-facing roof is partly shaded by a neighbor's tall pear tree. We asked for a shade review before choosing between the two array sizes on the household's preliminary quote.

QC-8 survey at 8 Quarry Close: the household wants a solar layout that works with the slate roof. The installer has proposed a smaller array near the chimney and requested closer photographs of the existing slates.

AW-H quote notes: the main house at 14 Alder Walk has an east-facing tiled roof. The proposed cable route reaches an inverter position in the utility-room cupboard. I asked the installer to verify that route before revising the equipment allowance.
AW-S planning note: the detached studio at 14 Alder Walk has a flat roof and its own proposed inverter position by the pottery sink. The roof sketch shows a low vent that constrains the first layout.

Linden Lane shade follow-up: the afternoon photo shows the pear tree shadow reaching the lower proposed row. Add the capture date and time to LL-22's review packet. We still need the installer's assessment of the two array options.
Saved reminder: 'Alder Walk inverter cupboard needs another look before accepting the quote.' It names neither the building nor the room, and has no job reference.

Main-house Alder Walk correction: the cupboard is in the utility room, not the kitchen. AW-H's survey sketch had copied a room label from an old floor plan. The east tiled roof is still the array location being reviewed.

Quarry Close follow-up: the chimney shadow crosses the proposed upper row in the morning photograph. Send the image with its capture time to the installer for QC-8's layout review. The photograph alone does not establish annual output.

Studio flat-roof survey: the low vent is farther from the rear parapet than the draft drawing showed. The installer will revise panel spacing for AW-S. The proposed inverter position remains beside the pottery sink pending their assessment.
LL-22 pear-tree photo timestamp added; the shade assessment is pending.
AW-H utility cupboard measured; installer still owes the revised route sketch.

Our neighborhood quote clinic will compare QC-8's chimney-shadow review with LL-22's pear-tree shade review. Bring the timed Quarry Close roof image and Linden Lane tree image so the installer can explain each household's outstanding layout question.
AW-S vent measurement corrected; revised studio panel arrangement has not arrived.
Loose quote annotation: 'Use the smaller array if the revised assessment supports it.' No address, roof description, installer name, or job number is present.
QC-8 slate close-ups sent; the chimney layout review remains open.

Correction to the Linden Lane call notes: the neighbor offered to share older tree photographs, not to prune the pear tree. LL-22's plan must use the existing shade conditions until actual changes are confirmed.

Homeowner log for the east roof at 14 Alder Walk: the installer visited the utility-room cupboard and took measurements, but the revised cable route has not arrived. The current quote still carries the old room label. I have filed the measurement email with AW-H and asked for a drawing that matches the actual room before we compare allowances. The roof photographs are complete enough for the present layout review; that does not resolve the indoor route. The next update should tell us whether the new drawing changes any of the quoted work.

Correction to the detached studio quote: 'sink cupboard' means the storage unit next to the pottery sink, not below it. Ask the installer to specify the assessed inverter position clearly on AW-S's drawing before the quote is accepted.

Quarry Close quote correction: the roof photograph labeled west was taken facing west from the garden; it shows the east roof slope. The installer confirmed the compass annotation needs fixing before QC-8's estimate is revised.
